correctness.rationale: For all c>=k>=3 and m_i>=2, the Alexander dual has faces occupying <=k-1 blocks. The explicitly defined block-mass map and uniform-barycenter section give a Γ-equivariant strong deformation retraction to sk_(k-2)(Δ_(c-1)). Its integral chain complex is the augmented exterior algebra on Z^c with contraction by summation; exactness leaves wedge^(k-1) U_c in degree k-2, other groups zero, with no torsion. Equivariant Alexander duality twists by the permutation sign on all N vertices and dualizes the lattice. The character formula follows from det(I+tπ)/ (1+t). For finite Γ, internal transpositions act by -1, forcing quotient rational acyclicity. Independently enumerated 8,672 equivariant Lefschetz traces and 5 mod-two homology calculations matched; no infinite proof is inferred from the code.

originality.rationale: The published all-chordal total-cut Theorem 4.13 already establishes exactly the same nonequivariant Betti ranks. This claim adds the complete natural integral Γ-lattice with the sign action on internal clique permutations and hook action of block permutations. The distinct 2024 ordinary cut-complex calculations have two clique components or complete multipartite graphs and do not imply the present c>=k>=3 total-cut module. Seven explicit published-finding corpus semantic searches and three relevant published sources were compared by implications, with no covering statement identified; nonindexed equivalence remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper may derive an equivalent equivariant Alexander-duality module for cluster graphs under other terminology.
The full literature was not exhaustively enumerated, so database absence alone is not used as novelty proof.

value.rationale: A canonical infinite family of highly symmetric chordal graphs shows that the known sphere-wedge count discards meaningful integral representation data. The theorem computes the full automorphism module for arbitrary component sizes, including the component Specht-hook factor, internal vertex parity, and vanishing rational homology of the full symmetry quotient; these properties are invisible from Betti numbers and are useful for equivariant topology and quotient invariants. It is a complete natural classification, not a finite unexplained invariant or a trivial restatement of the rank.
